questions.question_text: The product of a number and $5$ less than that number is $50$. Which option gives every possible value of the number?

options.why: Rejects the negative solution although nothing in the question restricts the number.
Reverses the signs of both solutions when reading them from the brackets.
Adds $5$ to $50$ instead of forming and solving a quadratic equation.

questions.solution_text:
Let the number be $x$.
$x(x-5)=50$
$x^{2}-5x-50=0$
Product $=-50$, sum $=-5$
Factor pair: $-10$ and $5$
$(x-10)(x+5)=0$
$x=10$ or $x=-5$

questions.question_text: What is the correct first step in solving $(x-8)(x+1)=10$?

options.text: Expand the brackets and rearrange to $x^{2}-7x-18=0$.

options.why: Applies the null factor law when the right-hand side is not zero.
Ignores the $10$ and treats the equation as though it equalled zero.
Splits $10$ into one factor pair, although many pairs give that product.

questions.solution_text:
The null factor law can only be used when the product equals $0$.
$(x-8)(x+1)=10$
$x^{2}-7x-8=10$
$x^{2}-7x-18=0$
